title: Monthly Card Credits Are a Part-Time Job
caption:
Face value is the number on the brochure. Usable value is what survives your calendar.

A $10 monthly credit can produce $120 over a year, but only if all 12 months cooperate. Each reset creates another chance to forget, miss the deadline, or buy something because the coupon is expiring.

The catch: effort is personal. Automatic credits tied to spending already in your routine can deserve close to face value. Narrow merchants, portal-only booking, and repeated reminders turn benefits into unpaid administration.

Count automatic annual credits first, discount anything that needs babysitting, and give forced spending a value of zero.

Full breakdown on practicalrewards.com (link in bio).

slides.heading: Face value is marketing
slides.body: Usable value depends on spending you already do and the effort required to collect it. Score your real routine—not your organized imaginary self.

slides.heading: Red means recurring homework
slides.body: Monthly expiration, narrow merchants, portal-only booking, and extra purchases turn a credit into a chore. Forced spending is not reimbursement.
